culture.title: See the Flying Squirrels at Brand New CarMax Park
culture.description: Richmond's $110m ballpark opened in April 2026 after a sixteen-year wait, with a 360-degree concourse and one of the biggest video boards in the minors.
culture.bonus: Do a full lap of the concourse without missing a pitch.

culture.title: Walk the Richmond Slave Trail to Lumpkin's Jail
culture.description: A riverside trail tracing the route enslaved people were marched through what was the second-largest slave market in the country, ending at the Devil's Half Acre.
culture.bonus: Read the Reconciliation Statue inscription at the end of the walk.

culture.title: Spend a Morning at the Black History Museum
culture.description: Housed in the old Leigh Street Armory in Jackson Ward, telling the story of Black Virginia from the Maggie Walker era onward.
culture.bonus: Walk Jackson Ward afterwards and find the Maggie Walker house.

culture.title: Tour Jefferson's Virginia State Capitol
culture.description: Thomas Jefferson designed it after a Roman temple in Nîmes, it has housed a legislature continuously since 1788, and the tour is free.
culture.bonus: Find the Houdon statue of Washington, carved from life.

culture.title: Stand in the Tredegar Ironworks Ruins
culture.description: The American Civil War Museum sits inside the foundry that armed the Confederacy, and tells the war from Union, Confederate and African American perspectives at once.
culture.bonus: Walk out to the riverside ruins after the galleries.

culture.title: Visit Poe in the Oldest House in Richmond
culture.description: The Poe Museum occupies the city's oldest standing building, with a walled Enchanted Garden and two resident black cats called Edgar and Pluto.
culture.bonus: Find both cats before you leave.

culture.title: See What the ICA Has Up This Month
culture.description: VCU's Institute for Contemporary Art holds no permanent collection at all, so every visit to the Markel Center is something you have not seen before.
culture.bonus: Go in knowing nothing about what is on show.

culture.title: Find the Fabergé Eggs at the VMFA
culture.description: One of the few major American art museums that is free and open late, holding the largest Fabergé collection outside Russia.
culture.bonus: Go on a night the museum is open late and stay past nine.

foodie.title: Take the Full Tasting Menu at Longoven
foodie.description: Ten to thirteen courses from a trio of chefs who started as a pop-up, still the most ambitious cooking in the city and a hard table to get.
foodie.bonus: Do the wine pairing rather than ordering by the glass.

foodie.title: Read the Whole Menu Out Loud at L'Opossum
foodie.description: David Shannon's gleefully camp Oregon Hill dining room, where the dish names are jokes and the cooking is completely serious.
foodie.bonus: Order the dish with the most absurd name on the menu.

foodie.title: Take a Bagel and a Cortado at Lamplighter
foodie.description: Richmond's long-running independent roaster, where the espresso is properly dialled in and the breakfast sandwich holds up.
foodie.bonus: Drink it in rather than taking it away.

foodie.title: Order the Steak Frites at Grisette
foodie.description: A small French-leaning room in Church Hill whose steak frites has become the dish people take visitors to eat.
foodie.bonus: Finish the frites before the steak is gone.

foodie.title: Sit in the Greenhouse Light at Jardin
foodie.description: Grisette's plant-filled sibling, a bright, green room doing a lighter menu and a brunch worth getting out of bed for.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the window table and order something you cannot identify from the name.

foodie.title: Build a Pastrami Sandwich at Perly's
foodie.description: One of Richmond's first delicatessens, still doing matzo ball soup, knishes and hot pastrami on Grace Street with a queue out the door at weekends.
foodie.bonus: Add the latke to the sandwich.

foodie.title: Eat Schnitzel in Church Hill at Metzger
foodie.description: Brittanny Anderson's German bar and butchery, a small dark room turning out chicken schnitzel and spaetzle that has kept a queue for a decade.
foodie.bonus: Drink a proper German beer with it rather than a cocktail.

foodie.title: Get There Early for ZZQ Brisket
foodie.description: Central Texas technique run through a Virginia lens in Scott's Addition, with a brisket that people queue for and a hard sell-out most days.
foodie.bonus: Get the fatty end of the brisket rather than the lean.

foodie.title: Order the Full Plate at Mama J's
foodie.description: Velma Johnson's Jackson Ward soul food kitchen — fried catfish, candied yams, cornbread — cooked the way her mother taught her.
foodie.bonus: Get the catfish and the mac and cheese and do not skip the cornbread.

foodie.title: Order the Spread at Stella's
foodie.description: Rustic Greek cooking in the Museum District since 1983, run by the founder's daughter and still the room Richmond books for a good night.
foodie.bonus: Order enough mezze that the table runs out of space.

foodie.title: Buy Bread Straight From the Wood Oven at Sub Rosa
foodie.description: A Church Hill bakery that mills its own heirloom grain and bakes everything in a wood-fired oven, which you can smell from the corner.
foodie.bonus: Buy a loaf and tear into it before you get home.

foodie.title: Sit at the Bar at Alewife
foodie.description: Church Hill's unfussy seafood room, cooking the Chesapeake with almost no ceremony and turning up on national best-of lists anyway.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever fish the board says came in that morning.

chill.title: Take a Pedal Boat Out on Fountain Lake
chill.description: Byrd Park's three lakes, a carillon tower and a pedal boat dock, all a few minutes from the Museum District.
chill.bonus: Do a full lap of the lake without switching who is pedalling.

chill.title: Follow the Canal Walk Through the Old Basin
chill.description: A mile and a half of restored canal towpath through the middle of downtown, with interpretive plaques and almost nobody on it on a weekday.
chill.bonus: Read every plaque you pass without skipping one.

chill.title: Dig the Crates at Plan 9 Music
chill.description: Carytown's long-standing record shop, deep in used vinyl and staffed by people who will happily argue with your taste.
chill.bonus: Buy a record purely because of the sleeve.

chill.title: Browse the Stacks at Chop Suey Books
chill.description: Two floors of used books in Carytown, with a resident cat and an upstairs room that swallows an hour without you noticing.
chill.bonus: Buy a used book with someone else's notes still in the margins.

chill.title: Get Lost in Lewis Ginter's Conservatory
chill.description: Fifty acres of themed gardens and a domed Victorian glasshouse, routinely ranked among the best botanical gardens in the country.
chill.bonus: Find the treehouse in the children's garden and climb it anyway.

chill.title: Catch Golden Hour on the Quirk Rooftop
chill.description: A pink-hued arts hotel on Broad Street whose rooftop has been on national best-of lists since it opened, and is at its best an hour before sunset.
chill.bonus: Go up before the evening crowd and claim a west-facing seat.

chill.title: Wander the Knot Garden at Agecroft Hall
chill.description: A genuine Tudor manor house shipped from Lancashire in the 1920s and rebuilt above the James, with formal Elizabethan gardens around it.
chill.bonus: Find the sunken garden and work out the knot pattern.

chill.title: See a Matinee at the Byrd Theatre
chill.description: A 1928 French Empire movie palace in Carytown, chandelier and all, still showing films for a few dollars with a Wurlitzer organ on weekend nights.
chill.bonus: Sit in the balcony and get there early enough for the organ.

chill.title: Do Carytown End to End on Foot
chill.description: Nine blocks of independent shops, vintage racks and coffee counters with almost no chains — the easiest low-effort afternoon in the city.
chill.bonus: Walk the full nine blocks and buy something from a shop you had never heard of.

chill.title: Walk the Bluff Path at Hollywood Cemetery
chill.description: A Victorian garden cemetery on a bluff over the James, holding two US presidents, a cast-iron dog and the quietest river view in Richmond.
chill.bonus: Find the iron dog at the Rees grave.

social.title: Drink Something Hazy at The Veil
social.description: The brewery that put Scott's Addition on the national map, trading in hop-forward cans people drive states for and a taproom that stays busy.
social.bonus: Drink the newest thing on the board, not the one you have heard of.

social.title: Take the Patio at Ardent Craft Ales
social.description: The Scott's Addition brewery locals quietly rate highest, with a walled beer garden that fills up the second the weather turns.
social.bonus: Get a spot in the beer garden without waiting for one.

social.title: Walk the Whole Scott's Addition Brewery Crawl
social.description: A former industrial district where a dozen breweries, a cidery and a meadery sit within a few walkable blocks of each other.
social.bonus: Hit four different producers in one afternoon without getting in a car.

social.title: See a Touring Act at The National
social.description: A restored 1923 theatre on Broad Street that books acts you would expect in cities twice Richmond's size, with sight lines to match.
social.bonus: Get on the floor rather than staying up on the mezzanine.

social.title: Eat and Drink at Väsen's Long Bar
social.description: Scandinavian-leaning beer in a converted Scott's Addition warehouse, with a huge open room built for standing around in groups.
social.bonus: Drink a style you would never normally order.

social.title: Get to Friday Cheers on Brown's Island
social.description: Richmond's outdoor spring concert series on the riverfront island, where the whole city turns out on Friday evenings from May into June.
social.bonus: Get there early enough to be on the grass rather than at the back.

social.title: Do All Three Days of the Richmond Folk Festival
social.description: A free October festival on the downtown riverfront with multiple stages of traditional music from around the world, and a crowd in the hundreds of thousands.
social.bonus: See a performer from a country you cannot place on a map.

social.title: Take the Long Table at Hardywood Park
social.description: Richmond's craft beer elder statesman, with a cavernous taproom, food trucks most nights and a gingerbread stout people plan their year around.
social.bonus: Find out when the Gingerbread Stout drops and put it in your calendar.

social.title: Get a Stool at The Jasper
social.description: Carytown's serious cocktail bar, named for a Richmond bartending legend, with a menu that reads like a history lesson and a room that fills fast.
social.bonus: Order a classic you have never tried and let them talk you through it.

social.title: Drink by the River at Triple Crossing Fulton
social.description: The bigger of Triple Crossing's two rooms, out in Fulton near Rocketts Landing, with a huge patio and some of the best lagers in the state.
social.bonus: Order a lager instead of an IPA and admit it was the right call.

social.title: Stand Three Rows Back at The Broadberry
social.description: A mid-size room on Broad with a small stage, which means almost every show feels closer than it should.
social.bonus: Talk to the band at the merch table afterwards.

social.title: Drink Above the Skyline at Kabana Rooftop
social.description: A downtown rooftop lounge with a full wraparound view of the Richmond skyline and a crowd dressed for it.
social.bonus: Get there before sunset and stay until the city lights up.

adventure.title: Take the Boardwalk to Texas Beach
adventure.description: A long wooden boardwalk over marsh and railway tracks that ends at a hidden sand and rock beach on the north bank.
adventure.bonus: Rock-hop as far out into the river as you dare.

adventure.title: Circle Brown's Island on the Riverfront
adventure.description: The flat green island in the middle of the downtown riverfront, linked by canal walk and footbridge, and the launch point for most of the city's best walking.
adventure.bonus: Follow the canal walk east until it runs out.

adventure.title: Cross the Footbridge to Belle Isle
adventure.description: A suspended walkway under the Lee Bridge drops you onto a 54-acre island of granite slabs, a flooded quarry and the best free sunbathing rocks in Virginia.
adventure.bonus: Find the old hydroelectric plant ruins on the island's south side.

adventure.title: Walk the Pipeline Under the Rapids
adventure.description: A catwalk bolted to a working sewer pipe beneath a railway trestle, with Class III rapids breaking a metre from your boots and a heron rookery overhead.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full length to the overlook without turning back.

adventure.title: Paddle the Dutch Gap Lagoons
adventure.description: A tidal maze of lagoons cut off from the James by a Civil War canal project, now a conservation area thick with osprey, eagles and cypress.
adventure.bonus: Paddle far enough in that you cannot hear a road.

adventure.title: Raft the Falls of the James Through Downtown
adventure.description: Richmond is the only city in America with Class III–IV whitewater inside its limits, and Riverside Outfitters runs you straight through it with the skyline in view.
adventure.bonus: Sit in the front of the raft through Hollywood Rapid.

adventure.title: Roam the Hundred Acres of Maymont
adventure.description: A Gilded Age estate given to the city, with a Japanese garden, an Italian garden, a waterfall and a bear — all of it free to walk into.
adventure.bonus: Find the waterfall in the Japanese garden and sit at the base of it.

adventure.title: Ride the Virginia Capital Trail to Jamestown
adventure.description: Fifty-two paved, car-free miles from downtown Richmond to Jamestown, through plantation country and tidewater farmland with pie stops along the way.
adventure.bonus: Make it at least as far as Charles City Courthouse before you turn around.

adventure.title: Watch the Sun Go Down from Libby Hill
adventure.description: The bend in the James said to have reminded settlers of Richmond upon Thames and given the city its name, still the best free view in town.
adventure.bonus: Get there early enough to watch the light change on the river bend.

adventure.title: Walk the Floodwall and the Potterfield Bridge
adventure.description: A flood-defence wall turned promenade, linked to a pedestrian bridge on old piers that puts you halfway across the James at eye level with the rapids.
adventure.bonus: Do it at dusk and stay for the skyline lights.

adventure.title: Trail Run Forest Hill and Reedy Creek
adventure.description: Quiet South Side woods with a stone dam, a lake and trails that connect straight through to the river park system.
adventure.bonus: Link Forest Hill all the way to Belle Isle on foot.

adventure.title: Float the James in a Tube
adventure.description: A lazy three-hour drift down the upper James with a shuttle at both ends and just enough riffles to keep it interesting.
adventure.bonus: Bring a waterproof speaker and get the whole group's tubes tied together.

adventure.title: Ride the Pocahontas Trail Network
adventure.description: Virginia's largest state park, twenty minutes south of the city, with purpose-built mountain bike trails graded from green to genuinely technical.
adventure.bonus: Ride one trail rated above your usual level.

adventure.title: Run the Buttermilk and North Bank Loop
adventure.description: Around seven miles of rooty singletrack along both banks of the James, linked by two bridges, entirely inside the city.
adventure.bonus: Do the whole loop without checking your pace once.

adventure.title: Claim a Rock at Pony Pasture Rapids
adventure.description: The city's favourite stretch of swimmable river — flat granite shelves, shallow rapids and a whole neighbourhood's worth of people doing nothing all afternoon.
adventure.bonus: Swim out to a rock nobody else has claimed.

adventure.title: Boulder the Cave at Peak Experiences
adventure.description: Fifteen thousand square feet of climbing terrain in the Brewers Row district, open from six in the morning, with a bouldering area big enough to spend a whole session in.
adventure.bonus: Project one problem until you send it, however long it takes.

8ball.title: Eight Ball: Scott's Addition Until It Runs Out
8ball.description: Start at any door in Scott's Addition and keep walking to the next producer until the neighbourhood closes on you — brewery, cidery, meadery, no skipping.
8ball.bonus: Get a stamp, coaster or can from every single stop.

8ball.title: Eight Ball: River First, Decide Later
8ball.description: Get on the James however you can — raft, tube, board or just a rock at Pony Pasture — then eat at the first place you find with a patio.
8ball.bonus: Do not look up a single review before you order.
